sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Use padding for internal breathing room
sketchBlocks.title: Use padding for internal breathing room

tryItExercises.title: Give the shared header balanced padding
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The shared header content touches its edges too closely, making the top of every page feel compressed.

**Task**

Keep the full checkpoint and add `header { padding: 1rem 1.5rem; }`.
tryItExercises.hint: Use the two-value `padding` shorthand: vertical spacing first, horizontal spacing second.

help.concept: Two-value `padding` can create balanced vertical and horizontal breathing room inside the same header box.
help.hint_1: Use the two-value `padding` shorthand: vertical spacing first, horizontal spacing second.
help.hint_2: Check the header across pages: the content should feel comfortably inset without moving the header away from the viewport.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Use margin to separate repeated links
sketchBlocks.title: Use margin to separate repeated links

tryItExercises.title: Separate existing navigation links with margin
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

Navigation links sit directly beside one another, so the menu is harder to scan and click comfortably.

**Task**

Keep all previous CSS and add `margin-right: 1rem;` to a `nav a` rule.
tryItExercises.hint: Add outside spacing to the links rather than `padding` the whole nav.

help.concept: Margin creates outside spacing between those link boxes without changing their text or internal area.
help.hint_1: Add outside spacing to the links rather than `padding` the whole nav.
help.hint_2: Preview the navigation: each link should have clearer separation while remaining on the same line when space allows.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Use borders to frame an existing image
sketchBlocks.title: Use borders to frame an existing image

tryItExercises.title: Frame the inherited profile image
tryItExercises.prompt:
**Problem**

The inherited profile image blends into the page and needs a simple frame without modifying the image file itself.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add an `img` rule with `border: 4px solid #cbd5e1;` and `padding: 0.25rem;`.
tryItExercises.hint: The asset stays byte-identical; create the frame entirely in CSS.

help.concept: A `border` plus a small amount of `padding` creates a deliberate image boundary while preserving the original image asset.
help.hint_1: The asset stays byte-identical; create the frame entirely in CSS.
help.hint_2: Check the profile image: it should gain a subtle framed treatment without any change to the PNG itself.

quizDraft.title: Check the first box-model decision
quizDraft.prompt: Which property adds space inside an element's border?
quizDraft.hint: Choose the property or layer whose location matches the question.

help.concept: Use the box-model concept named in the lesson rather than guessing from visual appearance alone.
help.hint_1: Compare what happens inside the border with what happens outside it.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that matches the exact CSS responsibility described.

quizDraft.title: Read a border shorthand
quizDraft.prompt: Which statements are true about `border: 4px solid #cbd5e1;`?
quizDraft.hint: Evaluate each statement independently against the lesson. More than one choice may be correct.

help.concept: A multi-select can have several correct statements.
help.hint_1: Check each statement independently against the prompt.
help.hint_2: Select every statement that is fully correct and leave the others unselected.

quizDraft.title: Select every correct box-model idea
quizDraft.prompt: Which values can be part of a border declaration?
quizDraft.hint: Evaluate each option independently against the definition in the lesson. More than one choice may be correct.

help.concept: A multi-select question can have more than one correct choice.
help.hint_1: Check each choice independently instead of assuming only one is correct.
help.hint_2: Select only the choices that satisfy the definition stated in the prompt.

quizDraft.title: Put the box-model idea in order
quizDraft.prompt: Order four-value spacing shorthand from first position to fourth.
quizDraft.hint: Start with the first conceptual or physical step and move outward or forward.

help.concept: Ordering helps make the CSS relationship explicit instead of memorizing disconnected terms.
help.hint_1: Identify the item that must come first.
help.hint_2: Then place each remaining item in the sequence described by the lesson.
